title: Aluminum minerals
process: Beneficiation -> alumina production -> electrolytic aluminum reduction
notes: Bauxite is a rock. Aluminum metal is not produced by ordinary ore smelting.

title: Antimony sulfides
notes: Processing must manage sulfur-bearing products.

title: Arsenic sulfides
notes: Toxic arsenic compounds require specialized handling.

title: Graphite processing
notes: Graphite is native carbon; not a metal ore.

title: Chromite processing
notes: Chromite is an important chromium ore.

title: Cobalt arsenides
notes: Arsenic-bearing mineral processing needs dedicated controls.

title: Oxidized copper minerals
products: Copper-bearing solution or concentrate; copper metal
process: Beneficiation or leaching -> copper recovery -> refining
notes: Suitable routes vary among carbonates, silicates and oxides.

title: Copper sulfide minerals
notes: Chalcopyrite and bornite can occur together. Pyrite may enter tailings.

title: Niobium and tantalum ores
products: Niobium or tantalum concentrate; refined metal products
notes: Different minerals require different separation routes.

title: Solid geological fuels
process: Sizing -> cleaning -> combustion or industrial use
notes: Coal and lignite are rocks, not mineral species.

title: Gem minerals
notes: Gem quality depends on characteristics beyond chemical formula.

title: Oil shale processing
notes: Kerogen-bearing sedimentary rock; not conventional crude oil.

title: Industrial minerals
products: Mineral feedstocks; glass or industrial products
notes: Quartz may support glassmaking. Not every industrial mineral is smelted.

title: Industrial rock processing
products: Aggregate; cut stone; lime or cement feed
process: Crushing, sizing, cutting or calcining as appropriate
notes: Rock recipes depend on composition. Limestone may be calcined.

title: Iron carbonates
notes: Siderite can be roasted before magnetic concentration.

title: Magnetite processing
products: Iron concentrate; iron metal; steel feed
notes: Recovery varies with mineral liberation and process settings.

title: Iron oxide processing
products: Iron concentrate; iron metal; steel feed
notes: Hematite and goethite require route-specific beneficiation.

title: Oxidized lead minerals
notes: Carbonate and sulfate lead minerals need tailored processing.

title: Lead sulfide processing
notes: Galena often occurs with other sulfide minerals.

title: Lithium phosphate minerals
notes: Specialized lithium chemical route; not simple smelting.

title: Lithium silicate minerals
notes: Spodumene and petalite have distinct processing requirements.

title: Magnesium carbonate minerals
notes: Magnesite is an industrial source of magnesia.

title: Manganese carbonates
process: Roasting or beneficiation -> reduction or refining
notes: Route depends on ore chemistry and target product.

title: Manganese oxides
notes: Manganese grades and gangue impact processing.

title: Mercury sulfide minerals
notes: Mercury is highly toxic; industrial controls are essential.

title: Molybdenum oxides
notes: Processing differs from molybdenum sulfides.

title: Molybdenum sulfides
process: Flotation -> roasting -> reduction or further refining
notes: Molybdenite is a principal molybdenum ore.

title: Native elements
notes: Processing depends on the element and deposit composition.

title: Native metals
notes: Native copper, silver and gold are already metallic minerals.

title: Nickel sulfide minerals
notes: Nickel-bearing sulfides may include iron and copper.

title: Phosphate minerals
notes: Apatite is used for phosphate production.

title: Potash minerals
notes: Sylvite is a source of potassium chloride.

title: Rare-earth minerals
notes: Rare-earth separations require multiple processing steps.

title: Silver sulfides
notes: Process choice depends on associated metals.

title: Iron sulfides
notes: Pyrite is not normally a primary copper mineral.

title: Tin oxides
notes: Cassiterite is a major tin ore.

title: Tin sulfides
notes: Mixed sulfide concentrates require selective processing.

title: Titanium minerals
notes: Rutile and ilmenite have different industrial routes.

title: Tungsten minerals
process: Gravity or flotation -> chemical conversion -> reduction
notes: Scheelite and wolframite may need different concentration methods.

title: Uranium minerals
notes: Radioactive materials require specialized safeguards.

title: Vanadium minerals
notes: Recovery depends on ore composition.

title: Oxidized zinc minerals
process: Concentration or leaching -> purification -> zinc recovery
notes: Oxides and carbonates do not behave like zinc sulfides.

title: Zinc sulfides
notes: Sphalerite is a major zinc ore.

title: Zirconium minerals
notes: Zircon can be used directly or processed further.
